title.scientific: Atmospheric Dynamics: Jet Streams and Global Circulation
title.algorithmic: Atmospheric Pattern Simulation using Vector Fields and Procedural Noise

scientific.concept: Earth's atmosphere is a dynamic fluid driven by thermal gradients, planetary rotation (Coriolis effect), and the distribution of continental and oceanic masses. Atmospheric circulation cells (Hadley, Ferrel, and Polar) determine global climate patterns.
scientific.analogy: The atmosphere works like a global heating system where the Equator acts as a hot radiator and the poles as cold zones. Warm air rises at the Equator, drifts toward the poles at high altitude, cools and sinks, creating circulation loops similar to convection cells in heated liquid.
scientific.real_world_example: The Jet Stream is a high-speed air current (up to 400 km/h) flowing west-to-east in the upper atmosphere. This 'river in the sky' dramatically affects weather patterns and air navigation, causing turbulence and diverting storm systems.
key_concepts: Coriolis effect: deflection of air masses due to Earth's rotation
Hadley cell: tropical circulation between Equator and ~30° latitude
Jet Stream: high-velocity currents in the tropopause
Atmospheric fronts: transition zones between air masses of different temperatures
Rossby number: ratio of inertial to Coriolis forces

algorithmic.algorithm: 2D vector field synthesis using Perlin curl-noise to generate incompressible flows

complexity.time: O(n) where n is the number of pixels/voxels in the simulation mesh
complexity.space: O(n) to store the velocity field

algorithmic.why_this_algorithm: Curl-noise guarantees the vector field is divergence-free (incompressible), a fundamental property of atmospheric fluids. Perlin noise provides organic and scalable patterns.

comparison.navier_stokes: Navier-Stokes is physically exact but computationally expensive for real-time
comparison.curl_noise: Curl-noise is artistically convincing and efficient, though not physically rigorous
comparison.spectral_methods: Spectral methods capture large scales but require more memory

parameters.name: noise_octaves
parameters.description: Number of noise octaves for detail

visualization_hints.color_mapping: Gradient from blue (cold/high pressure) to red (warm/low pressure)
visualization_hints.vector_display: Arrows or flow lines to show wind direction
visualization_hints.cloud_correlation: Clouds form where there is convergence and air ascent
